title: Isoptera (Blattodea: Termitoidae) 64-species x 16-locus design (PREPRINT-26 dimensions) vs. published phylogenomics
purpose: End-to-end seqnet -> RuNIE validation sweep at the dataset dimensions of PREPRINT-26 (isoptera-global-radiation-preprint): 64 species and 16 loci, with 15 mitochondrial loci sliced from complete/partial mitogenomes plus nuclear 28S rRNA. PREPRINT-26 only sets the taxon strata and quotas; it is not a validation source. Final trees are scored against inter-family and inter-subfamily clades reported in the peer-reviewed studies below. A clade is testable when the run samples >= 2 tips inside and >= 2 outside it, and recovered when the unrooted tree contains the corresponding bipartition.

design_reference.taxon_design: 4 outgroups (1 Blattidae, 1 Blattellidae, 2 Cryptocercidae), 6 basal termites (1 Mastotermitidae, 4 Termopsidae, 1 Hodotermitidae), 22 lower termites (10 Kalotermitidae, 12 Rhinotermitidae), and 32 higher Termitidae across 6 subfamilies (10 Macrotermitinae, 3 Apicotermitinae, 2 Cubitermitinae, 6 Termitinae, 8 Nasutitermitinae, 3 Syntermitinae).
design_reference.taxonomy_note: NCBI Taxonomy places all termites in epifamily Termitoidae (which ends in '-idae' and must not mask family/subfamily strata). NCBI places Blattella under Blattellidae (Ectobiidae synonym returns 0 GenBank mitogenomes), unites Zootermopsis/Porotermes/Stolotermes under Termopsidae (Archotermopsidae/Stolotermitidae return 0 GenBank mitogenomes), and encodes Cubitermitinae as 'Termitidae; Termitinae; Cubitermes group' inside INSDSeq_taxonomy.
design_reference.locus_interpretation: 15 mitochondrial loci (13 PCGs + 16S rrnL + 12S rrnS) sliced from GenBank mitogenomes (NOT srcdb_refseq[PROP]) plus mitogenome-anchored nuclear 28S (LSU_28S) = 16 orthologous phylogenomic loci. Multi-copy physiological nuclear paralog panels (GH9 cellulases, vitellogenins, CYP450s) remain in Stage 4 codon-selection tests rather than the species-level orthogonal panel.

sources.citation: Bourguignon, T., et al. (2015). The evolutionary history of termites as inferred from 66 mitochondrial genomes. Molecular Biology and Evolution, 32(2), 406-421.
Bourguignon, T., et al. (2017). Mitochondrial phylogenomics resolves the global spread of higher termites, ecosystem engineers of the tropics. Molecular Biology and Evolution, 34(3), 589-597.
Bucek, A., et al. (2019). Evolution of termite symbiosis informed by transcriptome-based phylogenies. Current Biology, 29(21), 3728-3734.
Inward, D., Beccaloni, G., & Eggleton, P. (2007). Death of an order: a comprehensive molecular phylogenetic study confirms that termites are eusocial cockroaches. Biology Letters, 3(3), 331-335.

Evangelista, D. A., et al. (2019). An integrative phylogenomic approach illuminates the evolutionary history of cockroaches and termites (Blattodea). Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 286(1895), 20182076.

scored_clades.name: Xylophagodea (Cryptocercidae + Isoptera vs. Blattidae + Blattellidae)

support.statement: Cryptocercus wood-roaches recovered as sister group to Isoptera (clade Xylophagodea)
Cryptocercidae + Isoptera forms the sister group to remaining Blattodea outgroups
Strongly supported sister relationship between Cryptocercidae and Isoptera

scored_clades.note: With 2 non-xylophagous cockroach outgroup tips (Blattidae + Blattellidae), this is the Dictyoptera outgroup split on the unrooted tree.

scored_clades.name: Isoptera (all termites vs. Cryptocercidae + cockroach outgroups)

support.statement: Termites form a strictly monophyletic clade nested inside Blattodea sister to Cryptocercus
Isoptera monophyly recovered with maximal posterior and bootstrap support
Mastotermes darwiniensis recovered as sister to all other living termites (Euisoptera)
Euisoptera maximally supported as sister to Mastotermitidae
Neoisoptera strongly supported as a monophyletic frontal-gland clade
Neoisoptera uniting Rhinotermitidae and Termitidae recovered with full support

scored_clades.name: Termitidae (all six sampled higher termite subfamilies)

support.statement: Higher termites (Termitidae) form a strictly monophyletic crown clade nested inside paraphyletic Rhinotermitidae
Monophyly of Termitidae maximally supported across mitochondrial genomes
Termitidae maximally supported across all transcriptomic datasets

scored_clades.name: Non-Macrotermitinae Termitidae (sister clade to basal Macrotermitinae)

support.statement: Macrotermitinae branched at the base of Termitidae, sister to all other higher termite subfamilies
All non-Macrotermitinae/Sphaerotermitinae subfamilies form a strongly supported clade sister to Macrotermitinae
Macrotermitinae + Sphaerotermitinae sister to the remaining crown Termitidae

report_only_clades.name: Rhinotermitidae (monophyly check)
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Known to be paraphyletic with respect to Termitidae in Bourguignon2015 and Bucek2019 (Heterotermes + Coptotermes + Reticulitermes are closer to Termitidae than to basal Rhinotermitidae genera).

report_only_clades.name: Termitinae (monophyly check)
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Known to be non-monophyletic/paraphyletic across Cubitermitinae, Syntermitinae, and Nasutitermitinae in Bourguignon2015, Bourguignon2017, and Bucek2019.

report_only_clades.name: Nasutitermitinae + Syntermitinae
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Relationship between Nasutitermitinae, Syntermitinae, and Amitermes/Termitinae clades differs between Bourguignon2017 mitogenomes and Bucek2019 transcriptomes.

report_only_clades.name: Cryptocercidae
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Single-stratum monophyly check (not an inter-family benchmark clade).

report_only_clades.name: Termopsidae
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Single-stratum paraphyletic assemblage in Bourguignon2015 / Bucek2019 (Archotermopsidae + Stolotermitidae + Hodotermitidae grade).
